meta.title: Green Ecolution | Measure. Understand. Act.
meta.description: Green Ecolution from Flensburg is developing an open platform that turns measurements into operations. We started with demand-based irrigation of urban trees.

hero.description: Sensors in the soil show which trees need water, and route planning sends your team straight there. Irrigation is only the beginning.

award.title: Winner of the 2026 Digitalisierungspreis of Schleswig-Holstein
award.description: In September 2026 the state of Schleswig-Holstein honoured Green Ecolution for resource-efficient software and demand-based irrigation. Digital minister Dirk Schrödter presented the prize in Kiel.
award.imageAlt: Digital minister Dirk Schrödter applauds two PROGEEK representatives holding trophy and certificate on stage, behind them a screen reading Green Ecolution

challenge.supportingText: Urban green spaces regulate the microclimate, promote biodiversity and strengthen a location's competitiveness. But persistent drought and a lack of digitalization threaten this asset. Many municipalities base their irrigation planning solely on the judgment of individual staff, with no data basis at all. Instead of demand-based irrigation, watering is done uniformly, wasting water while still not reaching every tree. Unoptimized irrigation trips also cause avoidable CO₂ emissions.

waterUse.description: Water is consumed by a mid-sized municipality for irrigation, often without a data basis and without demand-based control.

treeCost.description: is the cost of a single street tree. If it is lost due to insufficient irrigation, this damage alone covers the sensor costs for several years.

bedCost.description: can be the cost of a complete street bed, including civil works, substrate and infrastructure.

targetGroups.title: Who benefits
targetGroups.description: Green Ecolution is built for municipal operations. The benefit differs depending on the role.

municipality.description: Decisions about water, staff and vehicles rest on measurements instead of experience. Consumption and operations are documented per area and per tour, and can therefore be evidenced.

operations.description: Schedules and tours are generated instead of assembled by hand. The fleet, the teams and the review of actual consumption all live in one place.

field.description: The tour can be viewed in the app and can also be transferred to the navigation device in the vehicle. A traffic-light system on the map shows which trees and groups need water.

it.description: We run the platform, and where preferred inside the municipality's own Kubernetes cluster. Open interfaces, a plug-in system and open source keep the data and the control in house.

targetGroups.closing: Everyone else benefits indirectly: healthy urban trees cool the city climate and support biodiversity.
targetGroups.ctaAriaLabel: Go to the requirements on the product page
targetGroups.photoAlt: Two people at a young tree with a watering bag. One is crouching and using a tablet, the other is looking on.
targetGroups.photoLead: This is what it looks like day to day. The person watering sees what the site needs at the tree. The person planning sees it at their desk. Both work from the same data.

features.title: Green Ecolution at a glance
features.description: From sensor data collection through intelligent route planning to detailed analysis: all the features for efficient and sustainable green space management

dashboard.label: Real-time dashboard
dashboard.description: All key KPIs at a glance: soil moisture values, upcoming tours, team availability and vehicle status in one central dashboard.
dashboard.screenshotAlt: Dashboard of an irrigation group with irrigation status, soil temperature, last measurement and the water supply over time

grouping.label: Intelligent grouping
grouping.description: Group trees into irrigation units. Automatic calculation of water demand per cluster.
grouping.screenshotAlt: Overview of irrigation groups with status, number of trees and sensors per group

fleet.label: Fleet Management
fleet.description: Manage vans and trailers with water capacities. Automatic refill stops in route planning.
fleet.screenshotAlt: Form for adding a vehicle with licence plate, vehicle type, water capacity, driving licence class and dimensions

tourPlanning.label: Tour planning
tourPlanning.description: Optimized irrigation schedules with real-time status: from “planned” through “active” to “completed”.
tourPlanning.linkAriaLabel: Go to the route optimisation page
tourPlanning.screenshotAlt: Operations board with the columns suggestions, planned, en route and done

teamManagement.label: Team management
teamManagement.description: Manage drivers by license class and availability. Optimize deployment planning.
teamManagement.screenshotAlt: Team management with staff, roles, availability and driving licence classes

analysis.label: Post-analysis
analysis.description: Document actual water consumption per cluster and tour. Analyze trends and optimize future planning based on data.
analysis.screenshotAlt: Evaluation page with the number of irrigation groups, trees, sensors and watering plans as well as the water consumption

sensorProbe.illustrationAriaLabel: Schematic diagram of a soil probe measuring at several depths

soak.title: How deep does the water get?

shower.status: Only the top layer is moist. The probe reports moisture at the fine roots, the deeper measuring points stay dry.

midway.status: The water has reached the main roots. The deepest measuring point is still dry.

soak.status: The water has reached the root zone. All three measuring points report moisture.

sensorProbe.title: The soil probe
sensorProbe.description: Designed for use in public spaces. The probe measures at variable depths and so maps the root profile of a tree, from the near-surface fine roots to the deeper main roots. This makes it possible to see whether water actually reaches the root zone or only wets the surface.

installation.title: Installed by your own team
installation.text: The sensors are buried in the root zone of the trees by the staff of the municipal service centres themselves, without any external contractors. Installation is flush with the ground using standard soil augers, and maintenance work such as mowing is not affected.

sensorProbe.probeCarrier: The probe is one possible sensor, not the only one. The platform is built so that other sensors can be connected as well with some development work.
sensorProbe.availability: You get the probes directly from us, and your team can install them itself.

soilMoisture.label: Soil moisture
soilMoisture.description: Volumetric measurement of soil moisture at multiple depths

temperature.label: Temperature
temperature.description: Measurement of soil temperature for precise irrigation recommendations

sensorProbe.photoAlt: Installing a soil probe at a tree site: a worker in high-visibility clothing opens the hole prepared by the earth auger, with the probe and its cable held ready beside it.
sensorProbe.photoCaption: Installed together with the municipal service centre of Flensburg.

sensorSetup.title: Ready for use on site in a few steps
sensorSetup.description: A mobile app is already available for the setup: scanning the QR code on the sensor is all it takes to assign it to its tree and location and connect it to the platform. This way, a sensor is ready for use on site in just a few steps.
sensorSetup.photoAlt: A hand holds a LoRaWAN sensor with a QR code, next to it a smartphone shows the first step of the sensor setup in the Green Ecolution app.
sensorSetup.photoCaption: Setting up a sensor with the mobile app.

videos.title: Get to know Green Ecolution through video
videos.description: Two films show what we are working on: the State of Schleswig-Holstein's video on our Digitalisierungspreis 2026 award and the television piece public broadcaster NDR filmed about the project.

award.title: Digitalisierungspreis 2026
award.description: Green Ecolution received the Green Coding special prize at the State of Schleswig-Holstein's Digitalisierungspreis 2026. The state's video introduces the project and the open source solution for needs-based irrigation. It is in German.
award.posterAlt: A project member holding a soil moisture sensor, with a young street tree and a flatbed truck with a water tank in the background

ndr.title: NDR feature
ndr.description: In August 2026 the Schleswig-Holstein Magazin reported on urban trees that no longer survive the dry summers and spent a morning filming in Flensburg. The piece shows a soil moisture sensor going into the ground and how the city's technical operations centre plans the next watering run from its readings. It is in German.
ndr.posterAlt: View up into an oak canopy with the sun flaring through the leaves, the Schleswig-Holstein Magazin logo in the bottom left corner

workflow.title: The end-to-end workflow
workflow.description: Green Ecolution combines three steps into one platform. Sensors measure what is happening on site, the software turns that into a situation overview, and operations planning converts it into tours. We started with the irrigation of urban trees, and the platform is designed for further tasks.

measure.title: Measure
measure.description: Soil moisture sensors capture soil moisture and temperature at variable depths. The data is transmitted energy-efficiently via LoRaWAN.
measure.screenshotAlt: Transmitter unit of the soil moisture sensor with antenna and QR code, connected to the two soil moisture probes with their prongs
measure.installationAlt: Sketch of the sensor installation next to a young tree: the transmitter sits in a ground box just below the surface, the two probes are placed at 40 and 80 cm depth, each tilted 45 degrees towards the tree

understand.title: Understand
understand.description: A traffic-light system shows the current irrigation need on a map. Staff can see at a glance which green spaces need water. Time series enable detailed analyses.
understand.screenshotAlt: Map of Flensburg with coloured traffic light markers for the irrigation needs of tree groups and filters for very dry and slightly dry groups
understand.dashboardAlt: Detail page of a very dry irrigation group with soil temperature, last measurement and the water supply over seven days below the moderate and critical thresholds

act.title: Act
act.description: Automated dispatch and route planning generates optimized irrigation routes, taking into account water capacity, vehicle size, and road restrictions.
act.screenshotAlt: Route planning on the map with selected irrigation groups, the drawn tour and refill points

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about Green Ecolution

origin.question: Who is behind Green Ecolution?
origin.answerPlain:
Green Ecolution is a company based in Flensburg. {{director}} founded it together with {{group}} and runs it as managing director.

It began with a question from the City of Flensburg, which turned to Smarte Grenzregion with it. That became a master's project in Applied Computer Science at Flensburg University of Applied Sciences, together with the municipal service centre of Flensburg. In user tests with the service centre the application scored an above-average usability rating and was described as clear and manageable even by staff without an IT background.

We founded the company so that municipalities can use the solution in their daily work. You can find more on the About us page.

value.question: What value does Green Ecolution provide?
value.answerPlain:
Green Ecolution makes the watering of urban trees traceable. Sensor data shows which areas need water, and the scheduling turns that into tours without unnecessary trips. Watering this deliberately saves water, fuel and staff time, and decisions rest on measurements instead of experience.

For municipalities that means missing water becomes visible earlier, consumption is documented, and the solution can be operated in-house and developed further together, without being tied to a single vendor.

requirements.question: What does a municipality need to bring?
requirements.answerPlain:
For scheduling and route planning, the locations of the trees and areas, the vehicles you already have with their water capacities and the refill points across the city are enough. Sensors are not a prerequisite for this; they improve the prioritisation. Once probes are added they need a radio link: LoRaWAN today, or NB-IoT with a SIM card as an alternative.

Which data and which infrastructure are needed in detail is set out under the requirements on the product page.

openSource.question: What does the open source code give us?
openSource.answerPlain:
Three things, in practical terms. You can read and have audited what the system does with your data. There are no licence fees. And you are not tied to a vendor: the source code is public on GitHub and stays with the municipality even if it decides differently later.

Setup, operation and support are ours to handle. Open means you could do it yourself, not that you have to.

sensors.question: Is the system tied to specific sensors?
sensors.answerPlain:
No. The platform is modular, and our soil probe is one possible sensor, not the only one. Sensors from other manufacturers can be connected through The Things Network and the plug-in system. A new sensor type needs some development work, which we take care of. Connecting third-party sensors has not been proven in the field so far.

The soil probe we supply is built for public spaces and measures at variable depths. In the research project it contained a Watermark sensor for soil water tension and an SMT100 sensor for soil moisture and temperature. Today a series-produced model sits in the ground instead of the research prototype.

cost.question: What does it cost to use?
cost.answerPlain:
The software itself costs nothing; it is open source and free of licence fees. You pay for the probes, which you buy once, for the setup and, if we operate the platform for you, for the ongoing operation.

How this adds up is set out in the pricing model on the services page. We prepare a specific quote after an initial conversation.
